issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify Animal.messageOnFeed() returns a String (and examples show the method should return feed sound strings like "Arf Arf!", "Oink!", "Maah!"), but the solution implementation defines Animal.messageOnFeed() to return a FeedResponse object. This return-type mismatch is structural and can confuse students: they will implement messageOnFeed() as returning String (following the spec/template) while the provided solution uses a different type.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return type consistent. Either (A) change the solution to match the specification: modify Animal.messageOnFeed() and all overrides (Seal, Pig, Goat) to return String (and remove or stop using FeedResponse), or (B) update the problem statement and template to declare that messageOnFeed() returns FeedResponse (and document its semantics). Prefer option A to align with the UML/spec and the example expected strings.

issues.description: The problem statement requires Animal.messageOnFeed() to be an abstract method returning a String, but the solution implements messageOnFeed() to return a FeedResponse object (and adds a FeedResponse class). This changes the method's contract (return type) for the same conceptual operation (an animal's feed message) and introduces an unexpected type for students who are instructed to implement messageOnFeed():String. This mismatch can confuse students mapping the specification to the provided solution/template.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method signature consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) change the solution so Animal.messageOnFeed() returns String and update Pig/Seal/Goat to return the feed message String (remove or make FeedResponse optional), or (B) update the problem statement and template to specify that messageOnFeed() returns a FeedResponse (and document the class), so all artifacts use the same return type.
